hero.title: How True Aim reads a claim and decides it
hero.summary: True Aim separates reading from deciding. Language models read the documents and extract the facts. A deterministic decision engine then applies the policy wording and the cost rules, so the same claim always gets the same answer and every answer carries its reasoning.

problem.heading: Why a language model alone cannot decide a claim
problem.p1: Large language models are good at reading. They are also probabilistic: given the same input twice, they can produce different outputs, and they cannot explain a result in the terms a policy or a regulator uses.
problem.p2: A claims decision must be the same tomorrow as today, and it must name the clause, the figure and the rule behind it. So True Aim uses language models to read and fixed rules to decide.

reading.title: Reading layer
reading.subtitle: Language models and extraction
reading.description: Reads invoices, estimates, policies and correspondence in any format, extracts the fields and links each one to the page it came from.

deciding.title: Decision engine
deciding.subtitle: Deterministic rules
deciding.description: Applies the coverage terms, the exclusions and the payout order as fixed rules, so every decision is consistent and explainable.

auditTrail.title: Every figure has a source and every decision has a rule
auditTrail.description: Each extracted field traces to its source document and page. Each decision traces to the policy clause and the rule that fired. The record is produced with the decision, not reconstructed later.

control.heading: What keeps a person in control
control.subtitle: Five controls sit around the two layers. A person must always be able to understand, verify and override the result, because a regulated business stays accountable for every decision made in its name.

replayLogs.title: Replay
replayLogs.description: Any decision can be run again with the same inputs and gives the same output, so an auditor can reproduce it.

ruleTraceability.title: Rule traceability
ruleTraceability.description: Every coverage decision names the policy clause it rests on, so the adjuster sees which rules fired and why.

approvalGates.title: Approval gates
approvalGates.description: You set the thresholds for human review. High-value and unusual claims go to a person before anything is settled.

exceptionRouting.title: Exception routing
exceptionRouting.description: Claims outside a known pattern are flagged and routed to a person instead of being decided by the rules.

confidenceScoring.title: Confidence scoring
confidenceScoring.description: Each extracted field carries a confidence score, so the adjuster sees where the system is sure and where a check adds value.

items.question: Does a language model make the decision?
items.answer: No. Language models read the documents and extract the facts. The decision engine applies the policy terms and the cost rules as fixed logic. A language model takes part in a decision only where the rules do not settle the question, and that step is recorded like every other.

items.question: Can the same claim get two different answers?
items.answer: No. The decision engine is deterministic: the same inputs produce the same outputs, and any decision can be run again to prove it.

items.question: How does an adjuster see why a claim was refused?
items.answer: Each decision lists the clause that applied, the figures it used and the document and page each figure came from. The adjuster reads the reasoning, then confirms it or overrides it with a reason.

items.question: What happens when the system is not sure?
items.answer: Each field carries a confidence score. Claims below the confidence threshold you set, above the value you set or outside a known pattern are routed to a person.
